storage_homogeneous_mutation_source_cand.write_failure_timing_boundary: The narrow SomeWrite candidate remembers the first ACL rejection or Exact mismatch after successful native TEXT validation, then performs real later occurrence work until a hard error stops further SQL. An existing insert-only conflict, native error, DataLoss or resource rejection remains an immediate hard stop; sequential delete is unchanged. Explicit rollback precedes the inner error return. Rollback failure does not confirm rollback: it retires a pooled lease to prevent recycling after return, without disabling a direct repository. Existing outer pool deadline/shutdown policy can override the inner first error. Two held-tail and three early-stop cases are required source-execution observations. Full pgx prequeue/preparation/query-group and failing-occurrence native JSONB binding priority remain open. Controlled official Nakama PostgreSQL observations show a stale late Exact or token-matching/write0 Exact returning the first ACL rejection while the later tuple remains locked; Rust SELECT FOR UPDATE acquires that tuple lock. This observed conditional-lock countervector remains open alongside native isolation/retries, raw Runtime owners, hooks/index and full parity. No difference is normalized and no immutable-oracle or independent acceptance is granted.
